{{Quote|Although the Clone Wars were over, some people never seemed to get the message. The worst case of denial was Gizor Delso ''[''sic'']'', a Geonosian Separatist who'd somehow escaped Lord Vader's efforts to wipe out the remnants of the CIS.|Retired clone trooper|audio=GizorDellso1.flac|<ref name="BFII" />}}
'''Gizor Dellso''' was a [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] who worked for the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. [[Standard year/Legends|Years]] before the war [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|began]], he helped design a command signal that would shut down the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|droid army]] to prevent anyone from ever using their [[Battle droid/Legends|droids]] against them. At war's [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|end]], the same signal was ultimately used to deactivate the defeated [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]].

Although the Galactic Republic triumphed over the Confederacy at the end of the Clone Wars, Dellso [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|refused to surrender]] to the new [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. On the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], he reactivated a hidden [[Techno Union droid factory/Legends|droid factory]] near a former Separatist [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility/Legends|mining facility]] and began building his own private [[Gizor Dellso's army|droid army]], hoping to restart the war. However, the Empire sent the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] to Mustafar to [[Battle of Mustafar (Imperial Period)|eliminate Dellso]] and end his rebellion, resulting in the fugitive Geonosian's [[Death/Legends|death]] and the destruction of the secret [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Factory/Legends|factory]].

==Biography==
===Separatist stalwart===
{{Quote|By the time we'd made our way to the molten surface of Mustafar, it was apparent that Delso ''[''sic'']'' had been a busy little bug. All by his lonesome he'd found a previously-hidden droid factory, fired it up, and cranked out his own private army of battle droids.|Retired clone trooper|audio=GizorDellso2.flac|<ref name="BFII" />}}
[[File:Battledroids_BF.jpg|thumb|left|240px|Gizor Dellso helped design the shut-down signal that was eventually used to deactivate the Separatist Droid Army.]]
Gizor Dellso was a [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who [[Homeworld/Legends|hailed]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]]. At the behest of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], he served as one of the [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] who constructed a signal override apparatus that would shut down the conglomerate's [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|droid army]] in case enemies ever attempted to turn the [[Battle droid/Legends|droids]] against their masters. [[Standard year/Legends|Years]] later, Dellso joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]<ref name="db" /> along with his people and participated in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="BFII" /> The war ended when the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] was shut down by the same signal that Dellso had helped design, which spread through the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Separatist fleet]] via the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]].<ref name="db" />

Determined to [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|continue the fight]] against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Republic's successor state, the fugitive Dellso holed up inside a former Separatist<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility/Legends|mining facility]] on the planet [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]<ref name="BFII" />&mdash;the same [[Fortress/Legends|fortress]] where the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] had [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|slaughtered]] the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] at the end of the war.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Possessing [[Thief/Legends|stolen]] [[dataplan]]s for an experimental Imperial [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], Dellso needed protection while he planned his next move<ref name="db" /> and sought to keep Mustafar out of direct Imperial control.<ref name="Galaxies">[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> He reactivated a hidden [[Techno Union droid factory/Legends|droid factory]]<ref name="db" /> near the [[Mining/Legends|mining]] facility<ref name="BFII" /> and began producing new battle [[Droid/Legends|droids]] that he intended to use as his own private [[Army/Legends|army]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> Intimately familiar with the parameters of the droid deactivation device he had helped design, Dellso managed to countermand the shut-down signal.<ref name="db" /> He also built [[Confederate infantry prototype|prototypes of a new battle droid]] in the hopes of resurrecting the Separatist army.<ref name="Prima">[[Star Wars Battlefront II: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Battlefront II'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>

===Failed droid rebellion===
{{Quote|Lord Vader tracked him to Mustafar, and brought us in to finish the job. It seemed like a simple enough mission, but when we saw the fleet of droid ships hovering over the planet, we suddenly realized that Delso's ''[''sic'']'' denial mechanisms were a little more dangerous than we'd imagined.|Retired clone trooper|audio=GizorDellso3.flac|<ref name="BFII" />}}
Sometime between [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]] and [[12 BBY/Legends|12 BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> the Empire became aware of the threat that Dellso posed, and his location on Mustafar was discovered by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader. Seeking to end the rebellion before it could develop into a full-fledged war, Vader dispatched the elite [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] to [[Battle of Mustafar (Imperial Period)|eliminate Dellso]] and destroy his [[Gizor Dellso's army|droid army]]. In [[Realspace/Legends|space]] over Mustafar, [[Gizor Dellso's navy|Dellso's fleet]] confronted the Imperials, and his droid forces began boarding the 501st's [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]]. However, the 501st repelled the boarders, destroyed a number of [[Droid starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]], crippled a [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer]], and stole a [[Belbullab-24 strike bomber]].<ref name="BFII" />

[[File:Dellso_death.png|thumb|right|280px|Gizor Dellso is killed by the Imperial forces on Mustafar.]]
The 501st then landed on the planet and stormed the mining facility, where Dellso's army fought to fend off the stormtroopers and keep his rebellion alive, while the Imperials were determined to prevent the Clone Wars from reoccurring. After the 501st destroyed his prototype battle droid schematics, Dellso personally entered the fray, accompanied by other armed Geonosians and battle droids. Dellso rained fire down upon the Imperials with a [[Bulldog RLR]], but the 501st ultimately overwhelmed his forces and [[Death/Legends|killed]] the fugitive Geonosian by [[Blaster/Legends|blasting]] him.<ref name="BFII" /> As the Separatist holdout collapsed due to the sudden absence of leadership,<ref name="Galaxies" /> the Empire [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombarded]] Mustafar from space, destroying both the mining facility and Dellso's [[Factory/Legends|factory]]<ref name="BFII" />&mdash;and with it the last stubborn remains of the droid army.<ref name="db" />

Many of the 501st [[Legion/Legends|Legion's]] early missions remained classified for [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] until some of its members' [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] journals emerged.<ref name="db 501st">{{DB|organization|five01st|501st Legion}}</ref> One [[retired clone trooper]] [[501st Journal|recorded]] the 501st's mission to Mustafar, including the termination of Gizor Dellso and his failed droid insurrection.<ref name="BFII" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Some fools don't know when to stay beaten.|Unidentified 501st stormtrooper|<ref name="db" />}}
Gizor Dellso was an engineer who helped design the signal override apparatus for the Trade Federation Droid Army.<ref name="db" /> A Separatist stalwart, the fugitive Dellso<ref name="db Mustafar">{{DB|location|mustafar|Mustafar}}</ref> refused to surrender after the destruction of the Separatist Council at the end of the Clone Wars and made a failed bid to resurrect the droid rebellion<ref name="db" /> in the early [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="db Mustafar" /> A [[Limb/Legends|winged]] Geonosian, Dellso had [[Color/Legends|brown]] skin and dark [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="BFII" />

==Equipment==
Gizor Dellso wielded a Bulldog [[Missile launcher/Legends|RLR]] with a chassis akin to the [[Geonosian sonic blaster/Legends|Geonosian sonic blaster]] during the battle on Mustafar.<ref name="BFII" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Gizor Dellso has been defeated. Scratch one droid rebellion.|An Imperial trooper reports the death of Gizor Dellso|audio=GizorDellso4.flac|<ref name="BFII" />}}
[[File:Battlefront2.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Gizor Dellso first appeared in ''Star Wars: Battlefront II'' in 2005.]]
Gizor Dellso was created for the [[2005]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', developed by [[Pandemic Studios]] and published by [[LucasArts]]. Dellso features as the final objective in the two-part Mustafar mission, titled "[[W:c:battlefront:Mustafar Space - Preventive Measures|Preventive Measures]]" and "[[W:c:battlefront:Mustafar - Tying up Loose Ends|Tying up Loose Ends]]," as part of the game's "Rise of the Empire" [[W:c:battlefront:Campaign|campaign]].<ref name="BFII" />

In ''Star Wars: Battlefront II'' and ''[[Star Wars Battlefront II: Prima Official Game Guide]]'', the character's name is spelled "Gizor Delso,"<ref name="BFII" /><ref name="Prima" /> while the guide additionally misspells his last name as "Delsa" in multiple instances.<ref name="Prima" /> However, beginning with the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]],<ref name="db" /> all subsequent sources spelled his name as "Gizor Dellso."<ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="CSWE-Dellso">{{CSWECite|I|181|Dellso, Gizor}}</ref> The game also provides two different pronunciations for the character's name, spoken by the game's [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] narrator and an Imperial [[Trooper/Legends|trooper]] over [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] during the Mustafar mission.<ref name="BFII" />

Unlike other Geonosians in ''Battlefront II'', Dellso's in-game model does not feature wings while he is on the ground; however, his wings can be seen while he is flying. Additionally, Dellso's sidearm appears as a Geonosian [[Sonic blaster/Legends|sonic blaster]], but it operates as a Bulldog RLR, firing [[Missile/Legends|rockets]].<ref name="BFII" /> While ''Battlefront II'' and its game guide explicitly task the player with killing Dellso,<ref name="BFII" /><ref name="Prima" /> the [[October 28]], [[2005]] update<ref name="DBdate">{{SWArchive|url=databank/updates/news20051028.html|text=Missions of the 501st}}</ref> to the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] and the entry in [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''  for the 501st Legion alternatively stated that the 501st traveled to Mustafar to capture the rogue Geonosian.<ref name="db 501st" /><ref name="CSWE-501st">{{CSWECite|I|249&ndash;250|501st Imperial Legion}}</ref>
